title: Misalignment of LLM-Generated Personas with Human Perceptions in Low-Resource Settings

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the accuracy and Persona Perception Scale (PPS) scores of LLM-generated responses when adopting personas of opposing political parties in Bangladesh (Awami League and Bangladesh Nationalist Party) and comparing them to human baselines.

Comparing the accuracy and Persona Perception Scale (PPS) scores of LLM-generated responses for Male and Female personas answering culturally specific questions, identifying performance and representation gaps between genders.

Assessing the accuracy and Persona Perception Scale (PPS) scores of LLMs when adopting different religious personas (Muslim, Hindu, Christian, Buddhist) answering contextually relevant questions, with a focus on representation gaps for religious minorities.

Using dictionary-based sentiment analysis and word shift graphs to compare the emotional tone of LLM-generated responses with human responses, identifying a 'Pollyanna Principle' where models systematically favor positive vocabulary over negative terminology.
